# Installing Tools & Unpacking Files

## And general requirements before beginning to mod.

**Part 1**

Modding Dark Descent is a process that’s a little convoluted. Without any official mod support from Tindalos the prospective modder must rely on a selection of Tools generated by the community, such as Retoc-Tuw by Kregano and others such as uAssetGUI which was created for general UE modding. This guide will cover the very basics of what you’ll need to get started and will not cover the more intermediate steps. 

Let’s begin with creating a Folder Structure for ourselves. We’re going to need a kind of Master Folder which will house the various tools and folders that we’ll be using when modding Dark Descent. This Folder can be placed anywhere convenient and called whatever you want, it doesn’t really matter.

The first thing we’re going to want to add to your own Master Folder is a series of additional folders. We’re going to call these Folders “ExtractedFiles”, “uAssetGUI”, “Working” and “zModMyFirstMod”. We’ll leave these folders empty right now and fill them up as we go.

The first tool you’re going to want to download is a text editor capable of opening .json files. I recommend using [Notepad++](https://notepad-plus-plus.org/), I’ve been using it for almost a decade now and can wholeheartedly recommend it. Next you’re going to want to download [Retoc with GUI](https://www.nexusmods.com/aliensdarkdescent/mods/70), this is the tool you’ll be using to Repack files that you’ve altered into a readable format (.pak, .ucas and .utoc) as well as Unpack the various .pak files native to Dark Descent. Finally you’re going to want to get [uAssetGUI](https://github.com/atenfyr/UAssetGUI), this is your primary Editor for files for the moment.

When you’ve got the three of these downloaded, drop the uAssetGUI related files into its corresponding folder within your Master Folder. Put Retoc-Tuw.exe and retoc.exe in the Master Folder alongside the other folders **(it is important that these two .exes are placed in the same location)** as for Notepad++ just install it to your preferred location. You can add a shortcut to the program into your Master Folder if you’d like.

Our Master Folder should look something like the following now:  
![][image1]

With a general structure set up and the needed tools installed let’s move on.

**Part 2**

Start up Retoc-Tuw.exe and two windows should open, one command line interface  \- which for the purpose of this tutorial we will largely ignore \- and one UI for the program itself. The very first thing you’re going to want to do is go to the upper left, hit Menu and then click ‘IOStore retoc Unpack GUI’, this will switch the tool to an Unpack setting which we’ll be using to unpack the .pak files for Dark Descent. Below you can see some example pictures of my own Unpack GUI and how it looks. We’ll start at the top.

![][image2]  
Everything on your end should be set to look exactly like this. Next up we have Input and Output.  
![][image3]

In the Input Path you’re going to want to put in the location of the Paks folder in your Aliens Dark Descent install location, it should look something like ‘C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Steam\\steamapps\\common\\AliensDarkDescent\\ASF\\Content\\Paks’ for the Steam version. 

In the Output Directory we’re going to direct it to the ExtractedFiles folder in our Master Folder. Use the Browse button to locate this folder, but be sure you select ExtractedFiles as your folder and not accidentally the Master Folder itself, otherwise you’ll soon find unpacked files cluttering up your Folder Structure.

The Asset file name filter can be left empty.

Next up we have the last third of the UI.

![][image4]

**Make sure your checkboxes match mine as well as the Engine version override.** For Additional Options I included an example filter that you might find useful. The basic kind of Dark Descent modding is going to be editing values to make small changes. Stuff like changing the Damage of a Weapon, changing the Health of an Enemy or changing the Cost of an Upgrade. All of the files associated with these changes can be located in a Folder called Blueprint that’s contained within the .pak files. You could remove this filter if you prefer, but it will then unpack all of the files and folders within Dark Descent’s .pak files. Many of these are simply unnecessary for a beginning modder, even if we ignore the fact that unpacking every file is likely to take considerable time.

This filter can be edited by you depending on what you’re looking for, but you need to make sure that if you use a Filter that you always have ‘-f’ at the beginning. To give another example, if you wanted all files related to the Sentry Gun you might put ‘-f Sentry’ in the Additional Options bar.

Regardless, with everything now set let’s hit ‘Run’ and unpack these files. As a **Warning** when unpacking, this tool will max your Disk Usage, so it might be best to get a cup of coffee while you wait. When it’s finished you’ll get a little pop-up telling you “Success\!”, and if you check the Command Line Window it’ll tell you how many files have been extracted and to the folder location.

With our Files unpacked we now have a Folder Structure to build future mods out of, many of the Files we’ll be editing with uAssetGUI and some familiarity with Retoc-Tuw itself. To satiate your curiosity you can open up uAssetGUI and try opening some of the .uasset files that were extracted by Retoc, but don’t go saving any changes just yet\!

**Wrapping Up**

Let’s briefly go over the two folders in our Master Folder that I have yet to mention, as well as the Repack GUI for Retoc. These will be covered more extensively in the guide for creating your first mod.

So, what’s the ‘Working’ folder for? Well in here you’re going to be copy & pasting the files that you want to edit, rather than editing the files you just extracted. If your computer is anything like mine it was probably unusable during the Unpacking process and having to Unpack again if you mess up somewhere would be inconvenient, to say the least. So instead we’ll be putting the files that we want to edit into the ‘Working’ folder and editing them with uAssetGUI. While uAssetGUI does create backups of files you edit, it’s better to keep the ExtractedFiles folder clear of this excess clutter. Of course, you don’t *have* to do this, but it is my recommendation that you do or at the very least institute some other method of ensuring that if you mess up you’re not inconvenienced too much by it.

As for the ‘zModMyFirstMod’ folder, this is where you’ll be mimicking the Folder and File Structure within the ExtractedFiles folder when you want to Repack your mod into a .pak file using Retoc-Tuw. The naming convention of the Folder is important and this, along with the Repacking process itself, will be covered in greater detail in a separate guide.
